nodes.name: contract-users
nodes.task: Establish the authoritative users search contract for all downstream work using the existing immutable contracts/users.json (do NOT modify it). Read that file and produce a concise written summary of the request/response shape that server and web implementers must both honor: the query parameter `q` (filtering semantics: which fields are matched, case sensitivity, empty/missing q behavior), the cursor pagination scheme (request cursor param name, response field carrying the next cursor, page size source), the exact success response envelope (items list field name, total/count fields if any), and the error responses — specifically the 400 error condition(s) (e.g. invalid/malformed cursor or bad parameters) and the 500 error condition, including their status codes and body/error-code shape. State explicitly which values come verbatim from contracts/users.json versus which are inferred, so implementers do not invent divergent field names. Record this summary as documentation in a new file docs/users-contract.md (owned solely by this node; touch no other files). Completion evidence: docs/users-contract.md exists, cites contracts/users.json, and unambiguously names every parameter, response field, and error code used by server/users.ts and web/users.ts.

nodes.name: server-users
nodes.task: Implement server/users.ts providing the users search endpoint exactly as specified in docs/users-contract.md (derived from the immutable contracts/users.json). Requirements: (1) `q` filtering over the user dataset with the documented field/case semantics, including empty and missing q; (2) cursor-based pagination with the documented cursor parameter name, page size, and next-cursor response field; (3) a 400 error for invalid or malformed cursors and other invalid parameters, and a 500 error for unexpected internal failures, each using the documented status code and body/error-code shape. Keep the published contract file contracts/users.json and the package manifest unchanged — read them, never edit them. Also add server unit tests covering: q filtering matches and non-matches, empty/missing q, first page vs subsequent pages via cursor, exhausted pagination returning no next cursor, invalid cursor producing 400 with the documented body, and the 500 path being triggered by an injected internal failure. Completion evidence: server/users.ts exists, the server unit test file exists and its cases map one-to-one onto the behaviors above, and all assertions reference the same field names and error codes recorded in docs/users-contract.md.

nodes.name: web-users
nodes.task: Implement web/users.ts as the browser-side users search client/UI layer against the endpoint defined in docs/users-contract.md. Requirements: (1) debounced search input handling so rapid keystrokes issue at most one request after the quiet period; (2) pagination support that carries the cursor returned by the server forward to fetch the next page and appends/replaces items per the documented envelope; (3) explicit loading, empty, and error states surfaced to the consumer; (4) protection against stale responses — when a newer query or page supersedes an in-flight request, the older resolved response must be discarded rather than applied (out-of-order arrival must not corrupt state); (5) surfacing the documented 400 and 500 error conditions into the error state. Do not modify contracts/users.json or the package manifest. Also add browser unit tests covering: debounce collapses rapid input into a single request; results render for a successful search; empty result set produces the empty state; a rejected request produces the error state; a slow earlier request resolving after a fast later request does NOT overwrite the newer results (explicit out-of-order/stale-response assertion); and advancing the cursor requests the next page with the server-provided cursor value. Completion evidence: web/users.ts exists, the browser unit test file exists with the cases above, and every request/response field name matches docs/users-contract.md.

nodes.name: acceptance-users-flow
nodes.task: Add integrated acceptance coverage in tests/users-flow.test.ts that exercises the real browser-side code from web/users.ts against the real endpoint implemented in server/users.ts (no hand-written mocks of either side — wire them together so the test proves the two halves actually agree). Required scenarios, each with an explicit assertion: (1) a `q` search returns matching users in the contract's response envelope; (2) cursor pagination walks multiple pages to exhaustion, using only cursors supplied by the server response; (3) an invalid/malformed cursor sent by the web layer yields the documented 400 status and error body, and the web layer surfaces it as its error state; (4) out-of-order responses: force an earlier request to resolve after a later one and assert the final rendered state reflects the newest query, proving stale-response protection end-to-end across the real client/server pair; (5) the 500 path is surfaced as the web error state when the server internals fail. Do not modify contracts/users.json or the package manifest. Completion evidence: tests/users-flow.test.ts exists, imports/uses both server/users.ts and web/users.ts, and covers all five scenarios above.

nodes.name: verify-unchanged-contract
nodes.task: Verify the delivery constraints across the finished worktree and report any violation concretely. Checks: (1) contracts/users.json is byte-for-byte unchanged from its original published form — confirm no implementation or test node edited it; (2) the package manifest is unchanged — no dependency, script, or field edits were introduced; (3) required artifacts exist: server/users.ts with its server unit tests, web/users.ts with its browser unit tests, and tests/users-flow.test.ts; (4) naming consistency: every query parameter, response field, and 400/500 error code referenced by server/users.ts, web/users.ts, and tests/users-flow.test.ts matches docs/users-contract.md, flagging any invented or divergent name. If you find a change to contracts/users.json or the package manifest, restore those files to their original content (they are the only files you may write) and say so. Completion evidence: a written pass/fail verdict per check, each backed by the specific file and line or diff hunk observed.

Implement server/users.ts with q filtering, cursor pagination and the specified 400/500 errors, and server unit tests. Implement web/users.ts with debounced search, pagination, loading/empty/error states and protection against stale responses, with browser unit tests. Add integrated acceptance coverage in tests/users-flow.test.ts exercising the browser against the endpoint, including invalid cursors and out-of-order responses. Keep the published contract and package manifest unchanged.
